instrument_name: GDOL Rule 300-2-2-.02 Employer Tax and Wage Reports (mandatory electronic reporting, subsection 6)
authority: Georgia Dept of Labor via Georgia Secretary of State Rules and Regulations
figure_or_rule_carried: All employers shall submit tax and wage reports electronically unless expressly authorized by the department to file otherwise; failure may be treated as not filed (late penalties, loss of experience-rated rate). History line: amended F. July 20, 2026; eff. Aug. 9, 2026

instrument_name: SB 24 (2021-22 Regular Session) bill text amending O.C.G.A. 34-4-3 - existing-law text (scope exclusions)
article_or_section: 34-4-3(b)(c)(d) as reproduced in the bill (unstruck text)
figure_or_rule_carried: Existing 34-4-3 text as of the bill (2021): minimum wage 5.15 USD; chapter does not apply to employer with sales of 40,000 USD or less per year, five employees or less, domestic employers, farm owners/sharecroppers/land renters, employees paid wholly/partly in gratuities, HS/college students, newspaper carriers, nonprofit child-caring institution employees; and does not apply where an employer is subject to a higher federal minimum wage. Bill not enacted; currency in 2026 not independently confirmed

instrument_name: SB 61 (2023-24) Act 90 - repeal of sunset (subsection f) of O.C.G.A. 34-1-10 sick leave for care of immediate family
figure_or_rule_carried: Status history: Senate Date Signed by Governor 05/01/2023; Act 90; Effective Date 05/01/2023. Earlier sunset of 34-1-10 (SB 201, 2017: repeal July 1, 2020 unless extended) was extended by SB 408 (Act 378, eff. June 29, 2020) and removed by SB 61

instrument_name: Act 574 (SB 443, 2020) uniform garnishment procedures, amends O.C.G.A. 18-4-1 to 18-4-5 and others (Legislative Counsel summary)
authority: Georgia Office of Legislative Counsel (General Assembly)
figure_or_rule_carried: Act provides uniform procedures for garnishment actions, limits maximum disposable earnings garnishable in relation to certain educational or student loans, fixed time for continuous garnishments. Effective January 1, 2021. Summary only: the 18-4-5 text and DOR tax-levy specifics not read

instrument_name: Act 603 (SB 588, 2006) enacting O.C.G.A. 10-1-393.8 SSN use/display restriction (Legislative Counsel summary)
authority: Georgia Office of Legislative Counsel (General Assembly)
figure_or_rule_carried: Act prohibits the use or display of social security numbers except in specified circumstances; enacts O.C.G.A. 10-1-393.8; effective July 1, 2006. Statute text and pay-statement coverage not read on an official host

instrument_name: GDOL Employer Handbook DOL-224 (R-11-24): tax rate computation, new employer rate, loss of experience rating
article_or_section: Understanding Georgia's Tax Provisions - Tax Rates (handbook p.72, 74, 85)
figure_or_rule_carried: New employer rate 2.7 percent; rate cannot be reduced below 2.7 percent until benefits charged for 36 consecutive months ending on the computation date; delinquent reports 30 days after notice -> ineligible for calculated rate, assigned maximum rate allowable. Handbook prints no numeric min/max rate range and no sales threshold

instrument_name: 820 ILCS 115/2 definition of 'pay stub' and 115/10 pay stub furnishing, retention and electronic copies (Illinois Wage Payment and Collection Act)
figure_or_rule_carried: Pay stub = itemized statement of hours worked, rate of pay, overtime pay and overtime hours, gross wages earned, deductions, total of wages and deductions year to date; furnish each employee a pay stub each pay period; keep copy at least 3 years (paper or electronic); copies on request within 21 calendar days (twice per 12 months; former employees within one year of separation). 56 Ill. Adm. Code 300.600 (JCAR) is 'Payment of Wages' (check, voluntary direct deposit, voluntary payroll card) and carries no pay-stub content list

instrument_name: 56 Ill. Adm. Code 2720.100 employer delivery of 'What Every Worker Should Know About Unemployment Insurance' form on separation
figure_or_rule_carried: Each employer shall deliver the form to each worker separated for an expected duration of 7 or more days, at separation or, if impracticable, by mail within 5 days after separation to the last known address. Also 2720.132: employer notifies the Department when discharging for alleged felony or theft connected with work

instrument_name: City of Chicago BACP Minimum Wage page (Minimum Wage Ordinance MCC 6-105): July 1, 2026 general and tipped minimum wage
authority: City of Chicago Dept of Business Affairs and Consumer Protection
figure_or_rule_carried: As of July 1, 2026 minimum wage 17.05 USD/h (employers with 4+ employees); tipped workers 12.96 USD/h. 12.96/17.05 = 76.0 percent (17.05 x 0.76 = 12.958 -> 12.96), i.e. a 24 percent tipped credit; the percentage itself is not printed on the page read. Release states tipped rate steady until next scheduled increase July 1, 2028

instrument_name: Cook County Commission on Human Rights Interpretative and Procedural Rules, Paid Leave Ordinance (amended April 10, 2025)
authority: Cook County Commission on Human Rights
article_or_section: Sections 400.300, 400.500, 400.600, 400.800, 500.600, Date of First Allowable Use definition
figure_or_rule_carried: Accrual 1 hour per 40 hours worked (overtime-exempt presumed 40 h/week); 90 days after start of employment before first use; carryover of 40 hours or less may not be restricted (frontload of at least 40 h exempts carryover); unused paid leave paid out on separation if credited to a PTO bank, no later than next regular payday

instrument_name: 35 ILCS 5/203 Illinois Income Tax Act base income: federal AGI as modified (additions/subtractions)
figure_or_rule_carried: Base income starts from federal adjusted gross income as modified; the modification list in the text read contains no HSA or IRC s.125 addition (zero occurrences of 'health savings'), so federal exclusions flow through. IDOR Pub. 101 / IL-1040 instructions not opened (PDF)

instrument_name: 23 Pa.C.S. 4348 Attachment of income (child support income withholding)
figure_or_rule_carried: Attachment max = Consumer Credit Protection Act limits (4348(g)); employer must implement no later than 14 days from notice; payment to domestic relations section/SDU within seven business days of the date the obligor is paid; employer may deduct a one-time fee of 50 USD (4348(j)); employer liable for amounts willfully not withheld/forwarded (4348(k))

instrument_name: Act 161 of 2016 (P.L. 1210) electronic funds transfers, consumer protections and payroll card accounts (amending Act 173 of 1975)
figure_or_rule_carried: Payment of wages may be made by credit to a financial-institution account, including a payroll card account, if the recipient authorized it in writing or electronically; employer provides a written or electronic statement of earnings and deductions each pay period; payroll card: Reg E card, FDIC/NCUA-insured, not a condition of employment, prior written/electronic notice of options, switch to direct deposit/check honoured by first payday after 14 days. Section 7 states a 180-day effective clause for part of the act (exact commencement per section not resolved)

instrument_name: Philadelphia Code 9-4104 Accrual of Paid Sick Time (Promoting Healthy Families and Workplaces)
authority: City of Philadelphia (Philadelphia Code, American Legal Publishing official code library)
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum 1 hour of sick time per 40 hours worked in Philadelphia; cap 40 hours per calendar year unless employer selects higher; overtime-exempt assumed 40 h/week; use from 90th calendar day of employment; carryover unless employer provides at least 40 hours at start of each calendar year

instrument_name: PA DOR Letter Ruling PIT-06-005 'Health Savings Accounts; Withholding' (April 12, 2006)
authority: Pennsylvania Department of Revenue, Office of Chief Counsel
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer HSA contributions for a nondiscriminatory plan: excluded from compensation, no PA withholding; employee HSA elections made through a Section 125 cafeteria plan: excluded, no withholding; other employee contributions to an HSA (outside cafeteria plan): not exempt, withholding applies. Ruling is still posted on the PA DOR site; a later superseding ruling not searched

instrument_name: Act 18 of 2018 (P.L. 102) Local Tax Enabling Act omnibus amendments - Section 501 definition of 'earned income'
article_or_section: Act 18 of 2018 section 4 (amending LTEA section 501); sections 319 and 317 context
figure_or_rule_carried: Local 'earned income' = compensation as required to be reported to or determined by the Department of Revenue under section 303 of the Tax Reform Code of 1971 and its regulations, subject to listed inclusions/exclusions (i.e. same compensation base as PA PIT); collection forms/ordinances must be those promulgated by the department. DCED register cadence not read

instrument_name: PA Department of Revenue Wage-Garnishment page (Act 46 of 2003) - administrative wage levy for delinquent state taxes
figure_or_rule_carried: Revenue is authorized under Act 46 of 2003 to garnish wages of delinquent taxpayers; it can order an employer to withhold up to 10 percent of the taxpayer's gross wages and remit to the department. Statute text of Act 46 (72 P.S. 7345 cited in gap) not read

instrument_name: 34 Pa. Code 9.110 (weekly certified payroll statements) and 9.109 (payroll records) - Prevailing Wage Act regulations
authority: Pennsylvania Code & Bulletin (Pennsylvania Dept of Labor and Industry regulations)
figure_or_rule_carried: Contractors/subcontractors file under oath a statement each week and a final statement at the end of the work with the contracting agency certifying workmen were paid wages in strict conformity with the contract (9.110(a)); 9.109 records include worker name, address, SSN, craft/classification and hours per calendar day (retention period not read in the text captured)

figure_or_rule_carried: Status read 2026-11-06: introduced Jan 27, 2025 (PN 685), no votes or committee meetings listed; last action Oct. 21, 2026 Senate (remarks, Senate Journal). Not enacted; level: statewide minimum wage. Bill dollar figures not read

instrument_name: Act 151 of 2012 (P.L. 1209) Child Labor Act - hours of employment, 6-consecutive-day limit
article_or_section: Child Labor Act section 9(b),(d) and 16/17-year-old hours subsections; section 30
figure_or_rule_carried: Minors 14-15: not before 7 a.m. or after 7 p.m. (9 p.m. in school vacation), max 3 h on a school day, 8 h on a non-school day, 18 h in a school week, 40 h when school not in session; 16-17 in school week max 28 h/week and 8 h/day, not before 6 a.m. or after midnight (1 a.m. in vacation); vacation max 10 h/day and 48 h/week (hours over 44 voluntary); no more than six consecutive days (except newspaper delivery); act effective 90 days after enactment. Work-permit procedure not read in this pass

instrument_name: US DOL Women's Bureau 'History of Paid Leave in the United States' (March 2024) - list of states with paid family and medical leave programs
authority: US Department of Labor, Women's Bureau
article_or_section: Section on state paid family and medical leave
figure_or_rule_carried: 13 states and DC with enacted programs (CA, NJ, RI, NY, DC, WA, MA, CT, OR, CO, MD, DE, MN, ME); Ohio is not listed (inspected: the word 'Ohio' does not occur in the 26,785-character text). Dated March 2024; Hawaii TDI and the four state-administered TDI programs discussed separately; currency to Nov 2026 not established by this document alone

instrument_name: ORC 718.03 employer withholding of municipal income tax on qualifying wages (work municipality) and optional resident withholding
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer located or doing business in a taxing municipality withholds qualifying wages earned in the municipality x that municipality's rate (subject to 718.011 occasional-entrant rules); employer may also withhold for the resident municipality on the employee's request. Page shows 'Effective: September 14, 2016; Latest legislation SB 172 (131st GA)'

instrument_name: ORC 718.04 municipal ordinance/resolution content incl. resident credit for tax paid to another municipality
figure_or_rule_carried: A municipality may, by ordinance or resolution, grant a resident a credit for all or a portion of taxes paid to any municipal corporation; municipality not required to refund taxes not paid to it. So the credit rate/limit is set per municipal ordinance and is not a statewide figure; collector (city, RITA, CCA or state central collection) per municipality not read

instrument_name: Florida Constitution Art. X section 24(c) minimum wage and tip credit
authority: Florida Legislature (Florida Senate site, Florida Constitution)
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum wage reaches 15.00 USD/h on Sept 30, 2026; tipped employees: employers may credit tips up to the amount of the allowable FLSA tip credit in 2003. The 3.02 USD amount is not printed in this text (derivation 15.00 - 3.02 = 11.98 still rests on the 2003 federal figures); FloridaCommerce 2026 poster/announcement PDF not read

instrument_name: Texas Labor Code 204.005-204.006 major group contribution rate and initial contribution rate
figure_or_rule_carried: New employer's initial rate = the greater of (1) the 204.004 major-group rate for that year less one-tenth of one percent or (2) two and six-tenths percent, until the experience rate takes effect; major-group rate = average of rates paid by employers in the industry in the year ending Sept 30. The 2026 major-group rates are not in the statute, so the 2.70 percent figure cannot be re-derived here

instrument_name: NY Labor Law 590(2) notice of eligibility upon separation from employment
authority: New York State Legislature (NYS Open Legislation)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer must inform each employee in writing, on a department-furnished or approved form, at the time of each permanent or indefinite separation, reduction in hours, temporary separation or other interruption causing total or partial unemployment; form states employer name, registration number, address for requests. 12 NYCRR 472.8 text itself not read

instrument_name: NYS DOL 'Record of Employment' (Form IA 12.3) employer requirements page
authority: New York State Department of Labor
figure_or_rule_carried: Written notice required for any employee whose hours are reduced to 30 or less each week or who goes off the payroll, regardless of reason or temporary/permanent; content: employer name, NYS registration number, FEIN, payroll-records mailing address, instructions to file a UI claim; basis cited: NYS Labor Law 590(2). No numeric delivery deadline is printed
